name: Peter Jackson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Peter Jackson is best known for his "Lord of the Rings" and "The Hobbit" trilogies, which have grossed $6 billion worldwide.
The film director became a billionaire in 2021, after selling a chunk of his Weta digital film effects shop to Unity Software for $1.6 billion in cash and stock.
He made $10 million up front for each of the three "Lord of the Rings" films (2001-2003), with at least another 10% of profits earned from each film's box office receipts.
For the "Hobbit" movies, he likely made $20 million per film with 20% backend.
Jackson's Weta Digital used motion capture of the actor Andy Serkis to create the now-iconic on-screen visualization of the character Gollum.
forbes_facts: Sean Parker, the tech investor known for founding Napster and serving as Facebook's first president, had a 25% stake in Jackson's Weta Digital at the time of sale.

name: Kalen Jackson
forbes_bio: Jackson is the granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who acquired the Indianapolis Colts in 1972, and the youngest daughter of Jim Irsay, who ran the team from 1997 until his death in May 2025.
She and her sisters, Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Casey Foyt, inherited what Forbes estimates are equal 33.3% stakes in the franchise. They now rank among the richest female owners in sports.

Long before the three sisters were publicly named Colts co-owners in 2012, they had spent countless years around the organization, with their lives always revolving around the NFL schedule. Jackson, her sisters and their father all had matching horseshoe tattoos.

"He let us in on conversations at a very young age, and when I look back on it now, I'm kind of surprised," Jackson said of Irsay in June 2025. "But he trusted us, and he knew that we understood the seriousness of this job and the responsibility that we had. And I think we'll forever be grateful."

Jackson officially joined the organization in 2010 and currently leads its philanthropic arm, including mental health nonprofit Kicking The Stigma, while also holding the title of chief brand officer.

name: Alberto Cortina
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Alberto Cortina's fortune stems largely from construction company ACS, which is headed by fellow billionaire Florentino Pérez.
Alberto Cortina was married to Alicia Koplowitz, a billionaire who was a significant shareholder of the FCC construction group; they divorced in the nineties
Along with his billionaire cousin Alberto Alcocer, Cortina also had interests in banking, running Banco Zaragozano. They sold their combined 40% stake to Barclays in 2004.
forbes_facts: Cortina owns several ranches in Toledo, Spain, along with houses in Mallorca and Madrid.
The Panama Papers revealed that Cortina and his cousin Alcocer had offshore accounts in the Central American tax haven country.

name: Mao Geping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Mao Geping is chairman of his eponymous company Mao Geping Cosmetics, based in Hangzhou, China.
He took the company public in Hong Kong in 2024, raising over $300 million in the IPO.
The cosmetics brand competes with international labels in China's premium market, offering products such as $50 foundations and $30 eye shadow palettes.
Mao initially studied Chinese opera performance but later went into cosmetics. He set up his own brand in 2000.
The mogul's wife, Wang Liqun, is the company's vice chairman. His two sisters are both directors.

name: Park Dong-suk
forbes_bio: Park Dong-suk is the founder and CEO of Korean electrical transformer manufacturer Sanil Electric.
He set up the company in 1994 after working at Korean competitor manufacturer Yuil Electric.
More than 60% of Sanil Electric's revenue comes from the U.S. Its customers include utilities giants GE Vernova, PG&E and Duke Energy.
The company went public in 2024, raising 266 billion won ($190 million).

name: Anas Sefrioui
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2017)
forbes_bio: Anas Sefrioui is the founder and CEO of listed homebuilder Groupe Addoha, which has prospered thanks to government contracts.
He made his fortune developing low-cost housing in Morocco.
His daughter Kenza is the company's deputy chairman.

name: Wang Linpeng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2025); Hurun China (2018-2024)
forbes_bio: Wang Linpeng chairs Beijing Easyhome Investment Holdings Group, a home furnishings retailer.
Easyhome in 2018 operated or franchised some 400 home furnishing and building supply superstores in China.
Easyhome received investment of approximately $2 billion from a group that included China e-commerce heavyweight Alibaba in 2018.

name: Adrian Paval
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Adrian Paval and his brother, Dragos, own Dedeman, a leading Romanian construction materials and do-it-yourself home products retailer.
The $2 billion (sales) company's 57 stores stock some 60,000 products, ranging from tools and building supplies to furniture and appliances.
The brothers founded the business in 1992 with a single location in Bacau, Romania.
They also own shares of several publicly traded Romanian companies and a portfolio of real estate in Bucharest and the northern city of Cluj.

name: Gao Xingjiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Gao is chairman of Yongxing Special Materials Technology, a supplier of nickel alloy and stainless steel wire rods and bars.
Yongxing was established in July 2000.
Gao served in the People's Liberation Army Navy from 1981 to 1987.

name: Herbert Sy
forbes_bio: Herbert Sy is an adviser of SM Investments, a major conglomerate, and a director of SM Prime, the group's property developer.
He is a son of the late SM founder, Henry Sy Sr., and the second-youngest of six children.
His three brothers and two sisters all hold posts in the business, which spans banking, retail, real estate, mining, and hotels.
He is actively involved in the group's supermarket operations, which includes an investment arm.
He has an undergrad degree in management from De La Salle University.
In 2022, SM Investments agreed to acquire Philippine Geothermal Production in a $304 million, all-share deal in a bid to lower its carbon footprint.

name: Vitali Machitski
forbes_bio: Vitali Machitski traded timber and oil in 1990s and now controls publicly traded Vimetco, which has stakes in aluminum producers Alro in Europe and Zhongfu Industrial in China.
Machitski lost out to billionaires Mikhail Fridman and Viktor Vekselberg in the 1997 privatization auction of Tyumen Oil Company, one of the largest Russian oil companies.
In early 2000s he sold some refinery assets to Mikhail Khodorkovsky' Yukos and other buyers.

Machitski, a friend of Sergey Chemezov, the head of Rostec State Corporation, one of the largest weapon manufacturers in the world, controls companies that developed the Rostec-City business complex in Moscow.

name: Lidiya Mikhailova
forbes_bio: Lidiya Mikhailova and her sons control Cherkizovo Group, a meat producer founded by her ex-husband Igor Babaev.
In the 1980s, Babaev was elected as general director of the Cherkizovsky meat processing plant in Moscow.
He acquired all of the shares of the plant in the 1990s, during privatization, and started to buy other poultry and pig farms.
In 2005, the assets were merged into the Cherkizovo Group, which a year later went public on the London and Moscow stock exchanges.
Babaev gave all his shares to his sons, who manage the company. They own about 28% each; Lidiya owns about 15%.
